# Assignments {.unnumbered}

All graded work for the course is listed here. Dates and details will be posted as each item is released. The weights below follow the [assessment scheme](./course.qmd#assessment).

## Homeworks

**Best two of HW 1, HW 2, and HW 3: 20 marks.** Each homework score is first converted to a percentage; the best two percentages are averaged and scaled to 20 marks. The maximum points and problem format are specified in each sheet. There are **three homeworks**. The separate **mini coding project is worth 10 marks** and is not a fourth homework.
Problem sets are distributed as PDF; solution sets are posted after the
submission deadline. HW 1 is **graded for completion** — credit is for a genuine
attempt at every part rather than for correct answers. HW 2 onwards are **graded
on correctness**, with marks carried by the reasoning as much as the answer.

| # | Topic | Released | Due | Problems | Solutions |
|:---:|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|
| HW 1 | Random variables, joints, conditionals, Bayes | Mon 10 Aug 2026 | Tue 18 Aug 2026, in class | [PDF](./homeworks/hw1.pdf) | [PDF](./homeworks/hw1-solutions.pdf) |
| HW 2 | Distributions and maximum likelihood | Mon 10 Aug 2026 | Tue 25 Aug 2026, in class | [PDF](./homeworks/hw2.pdf) | [PDF](./homeworks/hw2-solutions.pdf) |
| HW 3 | From a known score to Langevin sampling (40 points) | Fri 23 Oct 2026 | Mon 26 Oct 2026 | [PDF](./homeworks/hw3.pdf) | After the deadline |

: {tbl-colwidths="[8,34,14,14,15,15]"}

Solution sets are worked derivations rather than answer keys: each problem states
the concept it is testing and derives the answer in full.

**HW 1–3 problem sheets and HW 1–2 worked solutions are available above.**
The HW 2 solutions also include the per-part marking scheme.

## Practice sheets

Not graded, and not submitted. Each sheet derives a small set of results in full and
ends with exercises — read it with a pen and redo the derivations yourself. These
are the computations the lectures assume you can do, so they are worth the time even
though no marks depend on them.

Practice 2 has a companion you can play with: **[The Walk Lab](./materials/walk-lab.html)**,
also embedded in the tutorial [The Random Walk](./tutorials/20-random-walk.qmd).

| # | Topic | Posted | Sheet |
|:---:|---|---|:---:|
| Practice 1 | Gaussian algebra and $q(x_t \mid x_0)$; conditional expectation as the squared-error minimiser; KL between Gaussians | Tue 18 Aug 2026 | [PDF](./homeworks/practice_01.pdf) |
| Practice 2 | The random walk: its exact law by counting, the heat equation, and a reverse step you can solve in closed form | Fri 21 Aug 2026 | [PDF](./homeworks/practice_02.pdf) |

: {tbl-colwidths="[12,52,18,18]"}

## Mid-semester examination

The mid-semester examination is **pen & paper**, worth **30 marks**, in the institute examination window **Sep 18–23, 2026**.

## Mini coding project

The mini coding project is worth **10 marks**, separate from the best-two homework component. Topic, deliverables, and deadline will be announced.

## Paper implementation

Paper implementation is worth **40 marks**. Candidate papers and scoped implementation exercises will be listed on the [Papers](./papers.qmd) page. The paper-selection process, deliverables, evaluation criteria, and deadline will be announced. This is the 40-mark assessment component in place of a separate end-semester written examination.
